> **Method-general analysis.** The selection engine for the main analysis is set
> once via `fs_subgroup_method` in the setup chunk — `"consistency"` (default),
> `"dina"`, or `"grf"` (with `fs_grf_selection` = `"tree"`/`"frontier"`). The
> headline fit and every downstream step — full bootstrap, MR,
> cross-validation, leave-one-out, and the Kaplan–Meier band — inherit that engine
> from the single fitted object, so the whole analysis re-renders under a
> different method by changing one knob. The comparative DINA-screening,
> standalone-DINA, and GRF sections that follow are fixed illustrations of the
> individual engines and are unaffected by `fs_subgroup_method`.

::: {.callout-note title="Two resampling procedures: FB and MR"}
Both correct the selected subgroup's effect estimate for selection bias, and
both appear throughout this document.

* **FB --- full bootstrap.** `forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()` re-runs the
  entire identification on each of `NB` nonparametric resamples, regenerating
  the candidate family every time, and applies the Leon (2024) Eq. 7
  correction. Cost scales with `NB`.
* **MR --- multiplier resampling.** `fs_mr_inference()`, reached via
  `forestsearch(mr_inference = TRUE)`, is a refit-free multiplier bootstrap
  computed inside the fit. It holds the fitted candidate family fixed and
  returns an infinitesimal-jackknife (IJ) interval. Cost is one vectorised
  `crossprod`, effectively independent of `NB`.

The two therefore target different estimands whenever the family regenerates:
FB marginalises over family regeneration, MR conditions on the realised family.
For the consistency engine with a fixed family they coincide to leading order,
which is what the FB-vs-MR panels below check.

**Where MR runs.** MR is computed once, inside the analysis fit itself. It does
**not** run inside bootstrap replicates or cross-validation folds. The argument
`mr_in_replicates` defaults to `FALSE` in `forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()`,
`forestsearch_Kfold()` and `forestsearch_tenfold()`, and each strips
`mr_inference` from the replicate call unless it is set. This document pins it
to `FALSE` at every one of those call sites -- the package default, so the pin
is a no-op that only makes the setting visible -- and never sets it to `TRUE`.
Every MR figure below therefore comes from the single fit for that engine.

Setting `mr_in_replicates = TRUE` restores the earlier behaviour, in which
`mr_inference = TRUE` was inherited from the parent call into every replicate.
That is worth doing only if a per-replicate MR object is wanted for its own
sake --- nothing downstream consumes one --- and it costs roughly 2.3x on the
main bootstrap at `NB` = 1000. The change is otherwise inert: with the outer
seed fixed, `TRUE` and `FALSE` give bit-identical resample indices, per-replicate
selected subgroups, and bias-corrected estimates.
:::

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")

# Initialize timing
timings <- list()
t_vignette_start <- proc.time()
```

## Parallel Processing Configuration

ForestSearch supports parallel processing for computationally intensive
operations (bootstrap, cross-validation).

```{r parallel-setup}
# PARALLELISM NOTES
#   * FS search -- forestsearch() parallelises the consistency search via its
#     own parallel_args; the plan is set per call and restored on exit.
#   * FB  -- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() uses %dofuture% with
#     .options.future = list(seed = TRUE), so each replicate holds its own
#     L'Ecuyer-CMRG substream.  It inherits the plan set here.
#   * MR  -- vectorised matrix algebra (a single crossprod over all draws), NOT
#     a parallel loop.  It needs no plan, only a threaded BLAS to benefit.  Do
#     not wrap it in a future.
#   * CV / LOO -- forestsearch_Kfold() and forestsearch_tenfold() pin each
#     fold's inner refit to plan = "sequential", workers = 1, so the fold loop
#     workers are the only ones in play.  No nested parallelism to guard.
# Every parallel block below is followed by plan("sequential").

# Worker count for every parallel block below: 80% of PHYSICAL cores (at least
# one).  This is a render-time setting, not the package default -- forestsearch's
# own .default_parallel_workers() is what applies the CRAN 2-core cap under
# R CMD check, and it is not in play here.
n_cores_total <- parallel::detectCores()
n_cores <- max(1L, floor(0.80 * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))
cat("Using", n_cores, "of", n_cores_total, "total cores for parallel processing")

# Number of bootstrap iterations
# Use 500-2000 for production; reduced here for vignette
NB <- 1000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation toggles (the slowest parts of the document).  Independent:
# run_cv  controls K-Fold cross-validation; run_loo controls leave-one-out
# (N-fold / OOB).  Either can be turned off without affecting the other.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   run_cv  : TRUE runs repeated K-fold CV (kfold-cv plus the diagnostic
#             tabulations and the identification plot).  FALSE skips all of
#             them; the cv-skipped-note chunk states so in the rendered output
#             and timings$kfold stays NA.
#   run_loo : TRUE runs leave-one-out / N-fold OOB.  FALSE skips it, the
#             loo-skipped-note chunk says so, and timings$oob stays NA.
run_cv  <- FALSE    # K-Fold cross-validation (kfold-cv + diagnostics)
run_loo <- FALSE    # Leave-one-out / N-fold OOB (oob-cv)
# K-fold CV with multiple iterations
# Use Ksims >= 50 for production
Ksims    <- 50
Kfolds_cv <- 10     # folds per iteration; feeds BOTH the call and the narrative,
                    # so the "Ksims x Kfolds" count in the prose cannot drift

# Pre-seed CV/LOO timings so the Computational Timing table is well-formed
# whether or not these run (skipped analyses report NA).
timings$kfold <- NA_real_
timings$oob   <- NA_real_

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-analysis identification parameters (tune each analysis independently).
#   sg_focus      : which candidate subgroup the selection step chooses
#   hr_threshold  : harm/benefit floor on the HR scale
#   hr_consistency: minimum consistency rate (consistency search only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main ForestSearch (consistency search)
fs_sg_focus              <- "effMaxSG"
fs_hr_threshold          <- 1.0
fs_hr_consistency        <- 1.0
# Uncapped.  The cap has no counterpart in the method: the candidate family is
# every conjunction of at most two conditions, less empty intersections and
# size/event failures, and selection ranges over that family.  Truncation
# applies a PREVIEW ordering, so the candidate that is optimal under the actual
# selection criterion can be discarded before it is ever evaluated.  Measured
# cost of removing it here: 73 extra candidates at ~4.8 ms each, under a second.
# It previously bound (pool 123 truncated to 50), so the FS label may differ from earlier runs --
# that is a result change, not a defect.
fs_max_subgroups_search  <- Inf

fs_conf_force <- c("er <= 0", "pgr <= 0")

fs_consistency_method    <- "resample"
# MR: a fast multiplier-bootstrap approximation of the
# bootstrap bias-correction, computed inside the fit and compared to the full
# bootstrap below.  It runs for whichever selection engine fs_subgroup_method
# names, de-biasing against that engine's own candidate family (it re-derives
# the per-candidate Cox dfbeta itself).
# run_mr : TRUE passes mr_inference = TRUE to every forestsearch() call, so the
#          MR de-biased estimate is computed inside each fit.  FALSE passes
#          mr_inference = FALSE and no MR compute runs at all; the MR rows and
#          tables then report that it was skipped rather than showing blanks.
run_mr <- TRUE     # add mr_inference = TRUE to the forestsearch call
mr_draws      <- 5000L    # multiplier-bootstrap draws for MR

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output directory for the Section 6.2 reproducibility payload written at the
# END of this document (manuscript Table + results overview).
#   NULL (default) -> alongside this .qmd, resolved at render time
#   or an explicit directory, e.g. "~/results" or "/abs/path/out"
#
# Pointed at ../rerun so this render writes NOWHERE NEAR the manuscript-era
# reference bundles that sit alongside this document.  This directory is
# read-only for the identifier-alignment re-analysis: gbsg_table_payload.rds
# is the comparison target, and rendering into the default NULL location is
# how a reference gets clobbered.  (The filename this document writes,
# gbsg_survival_multimethod_payload.rds, does not itself collide -- but its
# sibling ACTG175 document's does, so both are redirected for the same reason
# and by the same rule.)
results_dir <- "../rerun"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Selection engine for the MAIN analysis.  The headline fit, its bootstrap,
# the MR, CV/LOO, and the KM plot all flow from this single fit,
# so flipping subgroup_method re-runs the entire main analysis under that
# engine (each downstream step inherits the method from the fitted object):
#   "consistency" - the splitting-consistency search (default);
#   "dina"        - DINA performs selection (consistency search bypassed);
#   "grf"         - GRF performs selection (policy tree or DR-frontier).
# The MR de-biases against whichever engine's OWN candidate family,
# with re-selection matching that engine's selection rule.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fs_subgroup_method <- "consistency"  # "consistency" | "dina" | "grf"
fs_grf_selection   <- "frontier"      # only if fs_subgroup_method == "grf": "tree" | "frontier"
fs_grf_select_statistic <- "effect"       # only if subgroup_method=="grf" & grf_selection=="frontier": "dr" | "effect".
                                      #   "dr"     = native DR-score frontier winner;
                                      #   "effect" = re-rank the DR frontier on the inferential Cox HR (the
                                      #              statistic the MR de-biases).  No-op for the policy tree.
fs_grf_depth       <- 2L              # GRF depth (screening + GRF selection)
fs_dmin_grf        <- 4               # GRF DR-score screening floor
fs_dina_args       <- list()          # extra args forwarded to DINA selection
fs_dina_select_statistic <- "effect"    # only if subgroup_method=="dina": "dina" | "effect".
                                      #   "dina"   = native DINA tau-hat winner;
                                      #   "effect" = re-rank the DINA family on the inferential Cox HR (the
                                      #              statistic the MR de-biases).
# MR (main analysis): MR's de-biasing family for "dina"/"grf" is
# restricted to candidates competitive on the method's NATIVE statistic (DINA
# tau-hat / GRF DR-score).  NULL = use the recommended default, which matches the
# band to effect_neighborhood automatically (the band the engine selects within);
# give a number in (0, 1) to set the band explicitly, or >= 1 to de-bias against
# the full family.  Ignored for "consistency" (its maxcons rule already
# matches the search).
fs_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# (A) ForestSearch + DINA screening (consistency search selects; DINA only
#     contributes candidate cuts)
dina_screen_sg_focus             <- "effMaxSG"
dina_screen_hr_threshold         <- 0.9
dina_screen_hr_consistency       <- 0.8
# Uncapped, for the same reason as fs_max_subgroups_search above: no
# counterpart in the method, truncation under a preview ordering, and a
# measured cost of 12 extra candidates at ~4.8 ms each.  It previously bound
# (pool 42 truncated to 30).
dina_screen_max_subgroups_search <- Inf
# Screening cut set: FALSE => full DINA frontier; TRUE => only the single
# dina_subgroup()-selected cut (uses dina_screen_sg_focus / selection_rule).
dina_screen_selected_only        <- TRUE

# (C) ForestSearch subgroup_method = "dina" (DINA performs selection; the
#     consistency search is bypassed, so hr_consistency does not apply here).
#     The standalone DINA analysis (B) reuses these so (B) and (C) match.
fs_dina_sg_focus     <- "effMaxSG"
fs_dina_hr_threshold <- 0.90
# MR: the DINA de-biasing family is restricted to candidates competitive
# on DINA's native tau-hat.  NULL = recommended default (matches effect_neighborhood
# automatically); set a number in (0, 1) for an explicit band, or >= 1 for the full
# family.  Note: this only tunes candidate competition -- MR holds the forest
# fixed, so the full bootstrap stays the reference for DINA regardless.
fs_dina_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# (D) ForestSearch subgroup_method = "grf" (GRF performs selection via a causal
#     forest policy tree or DR-score frontier; the consistency search, LASSO and
#     DINA are bypassed).  Dedicated demo: always runs GRF regardless of
#     fs_subgroup_method, mirroring the standalone DINA selection (C).
fs_grf_demo_selection     <- "frontier"  # "frontier" | "tree"
fs_grf_demo_depth         <- 2L          # GRF tree / DR-pair depth
fs_grf_demo_dmin          <- 0.0         # DR-score harm floor (0 = permissive default)
fs_grf_sg_focus           <- "effMaxSG"  # -> GRF frontier/tree selection rule
# MR: the GRF de-biasing family is restricted to candidates competitive
# on GRF's native (RMST-based) DR-score.  NULL = recommended default (matches
# effect_neighborhood automatically); set a number in (0, 1) for an explicit band,
# or >= 1 for the full family.  Note: this only tunes candidate competition -- the
# MR holds the forest fixed, so the full bootstrap stays the reference for GRF
# regardless (a dominant DR-score winner can collapse the family to 1).
fs_grf_family_native_nbhd <- NULL
```



# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates the **ForestSearch** methodology for exploratory
subgroup identification in survival analysis, as described in
León et al. (2024) *Statistics in Medicine*.

## Motivation

In clinical trials, particularly oncology, subgroup analyses are essential for:

- Evaluating treatment effect consistency across patient populations
- Identifying subgroups where treatment may be detrimental (harm)
- Characterizing subgroups with enhanced benefit
- Informing regulatory decisions and clinical practice

While prespecified subgroups provide stronger evidence, important subgroups
based on patient characteristics may not be anticipated. ForestSearch provides
a principled approach to **exploratory** subgroup identification with proper
statistical inference.

## Methodology Overview

ForestSearch identifies subgroups through:

1. **Candidate factor selection**: Using LASSO and/or Generalized Random Forests (GRF)
2. **Exhaustive subgroup search**: Evaluating all combinations up to `maxk` factors
3. **Consistency-based selection**: Applying splitting consistency criteria
4. **Bootstrap bias correction**: Adjusting for selection-induced optimism
5. **Cross-validation**: Assessing algorithm stability

The key innovation is the **splitting consistency criterion**: a subgroup is
considered "consistent with harm" if, when randomly split 50/50 many times,
both halves consistently show hazard ratios ≥ 1.0 (for example if 1.0
represents a meaningful "harm threshold").

## Parameter provenance {#sec-param-helper}

Each `forestsearch()` fit carries `args_call_all`: the argument list the call
actually resolved to, kept in sync by the package's own `.sync_args_call_all()`
and used by `forestsearch()` itself for reconstruction. The helper below
reconciles that list against `formals(forestsearch)` at render time, so the
values reported are the ones the fit used, read from the fit rather than
restated in comments that can drift.

```{r param-provenance-helper}
#| code-fold: false

.fs_fmt_val <- function(v) {
  if (is.null(v)) return("NULL")
  if (is.data.frame(v)) return(sprintf("<data.frame %d x %d>", nrow(v), ncol(v)))
  if (is.function(v)) return("<function>")
  if (is.list(v)) {
    if (length(v) == 0L) return("list()")
    nms <- names(v); if (is.null(nms)) nms <- rep("", length(v))
    inner <- vapply(seq_along(v), function(i) {
      val <- tryCatch(paste(deparse(v[[i]], width.cutoff = 200L), collapse = " "),
                      error = function(e) "<?>")
      if (nzchar(nms[i])) paste0(nms[i], " = ", val) else val
    }, character(1))
    return(paste0("list(", paste(inner, collapse = ", "), ")"))
  }
  if (length(v) > 6L) return(sprintf("<%s[%d]>", class(v)[1], length(v)))
  paste(deparse(v, width.cutoff = 200L), collapse = " ")
}

.fs_fmt_default <- function(x) {
  if (identical(x, quote(expr = ))) return("<required; no default>")
  paste(deparse(x, width.cutoff = 200L), collapse = " ")
}

# match.arg-style values resolve to their first element.  Applied to BOTH sides
# of the comparison below: a value captured unresolved (grf_selection,
# grf_select_statistic) still sits at its default and must not read as differing.
.fs_collapse_matcharg <- function(x) {
  ifelse(!is.na(x) & grepl('^c[(]"', x),
         sub('^c[(]"([^"]*)".*$', '"\\1"', x), x)
}

#' Reconcile a fit's resolved arguments against forestsearch()'s formals
#'
#' @param fit A fitted `forestsearch()` object carrying `args_call_all`.
#' @param fn Function whose formals define the reference set.
#' @return One row per formal: the package default, the value the fit resolved
#'   to, and whether that value sits at the default.
fs_param_provenance <- function(fit, fn = forestsearch) {
  stopifnot(!is.null(fit), !is.null(fit$args_call_all))
  args <- fit$args_call_all
  fm   <- formals(fn)
  nm   <- setdiff(names(fm), "...")

  defaults <- vapply(fm[nm], .fs_fmt_default, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  used <- vapply(nm, function(p) {
    if (!p %in% names(args)) return(NA_character_)
    .fs_fmt_val(args[[p]])
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)

  eff      <- .fs_collapse_matcharg(defaults)
  eff_used <- .fs_collapse_matcharg(used)

  out <- data.frame(
    parameter  = nm,
    default    = defaults,
    value_used = ifelse(is.na(used), "(not captured)", used),
    status     = ifelse(is.na(used), "not captured",
                 ifelse(eff_used == eff, "at default", "differs from default")),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # forestsearch_main.R:1304 overrides these five under sg_focus = "maxeff" and
  # does NOT re-sync args_call_all afterwards (the package notes this itself at
  # ~2763), so what was captured is the value typed into the call, not the value
  # the engine ran with.
  if (identical(args$sg_focus, "maxeff")) {
    .ov <- c("pconsistency.threshold", "stop_threshold", "use_twostage",
             "max_subgroups_search", "minp")
    i <- out$parameter %in% .ov
    out$status[i] <- "captured BEFORE maxeff override -- not what the engine used"
  }

  out
}

#' Render a provenance table for one fit
# Selection-engine knobs: the formals that govern candidate generation,
# admission and selection.  The per-fit tables below show only these, and only
# where the resolved value is not the package default -- that is what a reader
# needs in order to interpret the fit.  The full 85-formal reconciliation for
# every fit is in @sec-param-appendix.
.fs_selection_knobs <- c(
  # engine and focus
  "subgroup_method", "sg_focus", "selection_rule", "effect_neighborhood",
  # admission thresholds
  "hr.threshold", "hr.consistency", "effect.threshold", "consistency.threshold",
  "pconsistency.threshold", "stop_threshold", "consistency_method", "fs.splits",
  # candidate generation
  "use_lasso", "use_grf", "use_dina", "use_twostage", "twostage_args",
  "conf_force", "conf.cont_jcuts", "collapse_cuts", "cont.cutoff",
  "maxk", "max_subgroups_search", "minp",
  # size constraints
  "n.min", "n.min.frac", "d0.min", "d1.min",
  # engine-specific
  "grf_selection", "grf_select_statistic", "grf_depth", "dmin.grf",
  "vi.grf.min", "dina_args",
  # post-selection inference
  "mr_inference", "mr_inference_args"
)

fs_param_table <- function(fit, title, knobs = .fs_selection_knobs) {
  pv   <- fs_param_provenance(fit)
  keep <- pv$parameter %in% knobs & pv$status != "at default"
  tab  <- pv[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  sub <- sprintf(
    "Selection-engine knobs differing from their package default: %d of %d such knobs, out of %d formals in all (forestsearch %s, read at render time). Full reconciliation in the appendix.",
    nrow(tab), sum(pv$parameter %in% knobs), nrow(pv),
    tryCatch(as.character(utils::packageVersion("forestsearch")),
             error = function(e) "version unknown"))
  # Only meaningful when the maxeff override actually fired; under any other
  # sg_focus nothing is overridden and the caveat would be false.
  if (any(grepl("^captured BEFORE", tab$status))) {
    sub <- paste(sub,
      "args_call_all is not re-synced after the sg_focus = \"maxeff\" override block",
      "(forestsearch_main.R:1304; the package notes this itself at ~2763), so the",
      "rows flagged as such report the value typed into the call rather than the",
      "value the engine used -- the render's own maxeff warning lists those.")
  }

  if (!nrow(tab)) {
    return(gt::gt(data.frame(note = "Every selection-engine knob is at its package default.")) |>
             gt::tab_header(title = title, subtitle = sub) |>
             gt::cols_label(note = "") |>
             gt::tab_options(table.font.size = gt::px(11)))
  }

  gt::gt(tab) |>
    gt::tab_header(title = title, subtitle = sub) |>
    gt::cols_label(parameter = "Parameter", default = "Package default",
                   value_used = "Value used", status = "Status") |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_text(font = gt::google_font("JetBrains Mono"), size = "x-small"),
      locations = gt::cells_body(columns = c(default, value_used))) |>
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = gt::px(11), data_row.padding = gt::px(2))
}
```


# Data: German Breast Cancer Study Group Trial

## Study Background

The GBSG trial evaluated hormonal treatment (tamoxifen) versus chemotherapy
in node-positive breast cancer patients. Key characteristics:

- **Sample size**: N = 686
- **Outcome**: Recurrence-free survival time
- **Censoring rate**: ~56%
- **Treatment**: Hormonal therapy (tamoxifen) vs. chemotherapy

## Data Preparation

```{r data-setup}
# Load GBSG data (included in forestsearch package)
df.analysis <- gbsg

# Prepare analysis variables
df.analysis <- within(df.analysis, {
  id <- seq_len(nrow(df.analysis))
  time_months <- rfstime / 30.4375
  grade3 <- ifelse(grade == "3", 1, 0)
  treat <- hormon
})

# Define variable roles
confounders.name <- c("age", "meno", "size", "grade3", "nodes", "pgr", "er")
outcome.name <- "time_months"
event.name <- "status"
id.name <- "id"
treat.name <- "hormon"

# Display data structure
cat("Sample size:", nrow(df.analysis), "\n")
cat("Events:", sum(df.analysis[[event.name]]),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(df.analysis[[event.name]])))
cat("Baseline factors:", paste(confounders.name, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Baseline Characteristics

```{r baseline-table}
create_summary_table(
  data = df.analysis,
  treat_var = treat.name,
  table_title = "GBSG Baseline Characteristics by Treatment Arm",
  vars_continuous = c("age", "nodes", "size", "er", "pgr"),
  vars_categorical = c("grade", "meno"),
  font_size = 12
)
```

## Kaplan-Meier Analysis (ITT Population)

```{r km-itt}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# Prepare counting process data for KM plot
dfcount <- df_counting(
  df = df.analysis,
  by.risk = 6,
  tte.name = outcome.name,
  event.name = event.name,
  treat.name = treat.name
)

# Plot with confidence intervals and log-rank test
plot_weighted_km(
  dfcount,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  show.logrank = TRUE,
  ymax = 1.05,
  xmed.fraction = 0.775,
  ymed.offset = 0.125
)
```

The ITT Cox hazard ratio estimate is approximately 0.69 (95% CI: 0.54, 0.89),
suggesting an overall benefit for hormonal therapy.


# Preliminary Analysis: Generalized Random Forests

Before running ForestSearch, we can use GRF to explore potential treatment
effect heterogeneity and identify candidate factors.

```{r grf-analysis}
t0 <- proc.time()

grf_est <- grf.subg.harm.survival(
  data = df.analysis,
  confounders.name = confounders.name,
  outcome.name = outcome.name,
  event.name = event.name,
  id.name = id.name,
  treat.name = treat.name,
  maxdepth = 2,
  n.min = 60,
  dmin.grf = 12,
  frac.tau = 0.60,
  details = TRUE,
  return_selected_cuts_only = FALSE
)

timings$grf <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
```

```{r grf-trees}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

# Display policy trees
# leaf1 = recommend control, leaf2 = recommend treatment
oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(grf_est$tree1, leaf.labels = c("Control", "Treat"), main = "Depth 1")
plot(grf_est$tree2, leaf.labels = c("Control", "Treat"), main = "Depth 2")
par(oldpar)
```

GRF identifies estrogen receptor status (ER) as a key factor, with ER ≤ 0
suggesting potential harm from hormonal therapy.


# ForestSearch Analysis




## Running ForestSearch

The selection engine for this main analysis is set by `fs_subgroup_method` in
the setup chunk (`"consistency"`, `"dina"`, or `"grf"` with `fs_grf_selection`).
Everything downstream — the full bootstrap, the MR, the
cross-validation/leave-one-out diagnostics, and the Kaplan–Meier band — runs off
the single fitted object and therefore inherits that engine automatically, so
the entire analysis re-renders under a different method by changing one knob.
The consistency search (the default below) performs an exhaustive search over
candidate subgroup combinations with up to `maxk` factors.

The parameters this fit actually used are not restated here. They are rendered
from `fit$args_call_all` by the provenance table immediately after the call
(@sec-param-helper), so they cannot drift from the code that produced the
results; the full reconciliation across all fits is in @sec-param-appendix.

::: {.callout-note}
## Selection criteria (`sg_focus`)

`sg_focus` chooses among the candidates that survive admission. This analysis
uses `"effMaxSG"`. The `eff*` spellings are preferred over the internal
Cox-flavoured `hr*` names because they carry over to GLM outcomes; both
normalise to the same rule.

**Foci with no band.** These rank all qualifiers directly:

* `"maxcons"` (alias `"eff"`) --- consistency argmax: highest `Pcons`, ties
  broken by effect. Canonical name `"hr"`.
* `"maxeff"` --- effect argmax over *all* candidates, ungated: key
  $(-\mathrm{hr}, K)$. No consistency condition is applied at selection, and the
  effect floor is disabled.
* `"maxeffCons"` --- effect argmax *among consistency-qualifying* candidates.
  The only focus for which first-passer early stopping is sound, because its key
  matches the enumeration order exactly.
* `"maxSG"` / `"minSG"` --- largest / smallest qualifier, ties by consistency.
  These are **not** spellings of `"effMaxSG"`/`"effMinSG"`: they rank by size
  among all qualifiers with no band at all.

**Foci with a band.** `"effMaxSG"` / `"effMinSG"` (canonical
`"hrMaxSG"`/`"hrMinSG"`) do *not* simply take the largest effect. Candidates are
first partitioned into a **candidate inclusion band**, then ranked within it by
sample size. The full sort for `"effMaxSG"` is five keys:

$$(-\texttt{in\_band},\; -N,\; -\texttt{Pcons},\; -\texttt{hr},\; K)$$

so: in-band first, then largest $N$, then higher consistency, then higher
effect, then fewer factors. `"effMinSG"` is identical except $N$ is minimised.
Only `in_band` depends on `selection_rule`; the sort itself is fixed.

**`selection_rule` draws the band.** `.compute_inclusion_band()` forms two
indicators and multiplies them:

| `selection_rule` | `in_nbhd` | `in_pareto` | `in_band` is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"neighborhood"` (default) | active | all ones | the effect band only |
| `"pareto"` | all ones | active | the frontier only |
| `"both"` | active | active | their intersection |

`in_nbhd` is a *relative* tolerance: with `effect_neighborhood = 0.10` a
candidate is in-band iff its effect is within 10% of the strongest effect among
the survivors. Setting it to `0` collapses the band to a strict max-effect
filter. `in_pareto` is the two-dimensional Pareto-non-dominated set on
(effect, $N$) --- candidate $i$ is dominated when some $j$ is at least as good on
both axes and strictly better on one. For ratio measures stored on the log scale
(GLM OR, IRR) both tests are applied after exponentiating, so the comparison is
on the natural scale; Cox HR is already natural.

**Scope.** `selection_rule` and `effect_neighborhood` are consulted *only* by
`"effMaxSG"`/`"effMinSG"`. For every other focus they are inert --- and this is
enforced, not ignored: passing a `selection_rule` other than `"neighborhood"`
together with a non-band focus is an **error**, not a silent no-op.
:::

```{r forestsearch-main}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

t0 <- proc.time()

fs <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis,
  outcome.name              = outcome.name,
  event.name                = event.name,
  treat.name                = treat.name,
  id.name                   = id.name,
  confounders.name          = confounders.name,
  potentialOutcome.name     = NULL,           # default NULL
  flag_harm.name            = NULL,           # default NULL
  df.predict                = NULL,           # default NULL
  df.test                   = NULL,           # default NULL
  is.RCT                    = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  seedit                    = 8316951,        # default 8316951
  est.scale                 = "hr",           # default "hr"
  # --- Screening engines (candidate generation) ---------------------------
  use_lasso                 = FALSE,           # default TRUE
  use_grf                   = FALSE,           # default TRUE
  grf_res                   = NULL,           # default NULL
  grf_cuts                  = NULL,           # default NULL
  grf_depth                 = fs_grf_depth,   # set in setup chunk (default 2)
  dmin.grf                  = fs_dmin_grf,     # set in setup chunk (default 0.0)
  frac.tau                  = 0.80,           # default 0.8
  vi.grf.min                = -0.2,           # default -0.2
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  tune_grf                  = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  use_dina                  = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  dina_res                  = NULL,           # default NULL
  dina_cuts                 = NULL,           # default NULL
  dina_args                 = fs_dina_args,   # extra DINA tuning (setup chunk)
  # --- Candidate-cut construction -----------------------------------------
  max_n_confounders         = 1000,           # default 1000
  conf_force                = fs_conf_force,           # default NULL
  defaultcut_names          = NULL,           # default NULL
  cut_type                  = "default",      # default "default"
  exclude_cuts              = NULL,           # default NULL
  replace_med_grf           = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  cont.cutoff               = 4,              # default 4
  conf.cont_medians         = NULL,           # default NULL
  conf.cont_medians_force   = NULL,           # default NULL
  conf.cont_jcuts           = list(er = 10, pgr = 10),           # default NULL
  collapse_cuts = TRUE,
  # --- Selection engine ---------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method           = fs_subgroup_method,  # set in setup chunk: consistency | dina | grf
  grf_selection             = fs_grf_selection,    # set in setup chunk (used when subgroup_method = "grf")
  grf_select_statistic      = fs_grf_select_statistic,  # set in setup chunk (frontier only)
  dina_select_statistic     = fs_dina_select_statistic,  # set in setup chunk (used when subgroup_method = "dina")
  sg_focus                  = fs_sg_focus,         # set in setup chunk
  selection_rule            = "neighborhood",  # default "neighborhood"
  effect_neighborhood       = 0.10,            # default 0.10
  # --- MR ----------------------------------------------
  mr_inference               = run_mr,           # set in setup chunk
  mr_inference_args          = list(draws = mr_draws,
                                   family_native_neighborhood = fs_family_native_nbhd),
  # --- Subgroup constraints -----------------------------------------------
  n.min                     = 60,                       # default 60
  d0.min                    = 10,                       # default 10
  d1.min                    = 10,                       # default 10
  maxk                      = 2,                        # default 2
  max_subgroups_search      = fs_max_subgroups_search,  # set in setup chunk
  # --- Thresholds (survival / HR scale) -----------------------------------
  hr.threshold              = fs_hr_threshold,    # set in setup chunk
  hr.consistency            = fs_hr_consistency,  # set in setup chunk
  effect.threshold          = NULL,           # default NULL (alias of hr.threshold)
  consistency.threshold     = NULL,           # default NULL (alias of hr.consistency)
  pconsistency.threshold    = 0.90,           # default 0.90
  consistency_method        = fs_consistency_method,
  m1.threshold              = Inf,            # default Inf
  minp                      = 0.025,          # default 0.025
  # --- Consistency search -------------------------------------------------
  fs.splits                 = 1000,           # default 1000
  stop_threshold            = NULL,           # NULL is what this configuration RESOLVES to, not a
                                              #   preference.  This call's sg_focus ("effMaxSG")
                                              #   normalizes to "hrMaxSG", and forestsearch_main.R:1403
                                              #   resets stop_threshold to NULL for that focus: a
                                              #   neighborhood band needs every candidate evaluated,
                                              #   so a truncated scan is unsound.  Any non-NULL value
                                              #   reaches the same NULL but warns on every render;
                                              #   passing NULL skips the reset branch outright (its
                                              #   guard is !is.null(stop_threshold)).  Named here so
                                              #   the resolved setting stays inspectable.
  use_twostage              = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  twostage_args             = list(),         # default list()
  max.minutes               = 3,              # default 3
  # --- Output / diagnostics -----------------------------------------------
  show_candidate_summary    = TRUE,           # default FALSE
  details                   = TRUE,           # default FALSE
  quiet                     = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  by.risk                   = 12,             # default 12
  plot.sg                   = TRUE,           # default FALSE
  plot.grf                  = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  # --- Parallel -----------------------------------------------------------
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

plan("sequential")
timings$forestsearch <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

# Fit-integrity guard.  NOT stopifnot(!is.null(fs$sg.harm)): a NULL subgroup is
# a legitimate outcome this document handles explicitly (see the *-no-subgroup
# chunks).  Assert only that the fit returned and captured its arguments, which
# every downstream provenance table depends on.
stopifnot(!is.null(fs), !is.null(fs$args_call_all))

# Guard for the GRF-dependent diagnostics below, read from the FIT rather than
# from the call, so it tracks whatever the fit actually resolved to.  With
# use_grf = FALSE no GRF cut is ever produced, and the bootstrap GRF-cut
# stability table would render a single "(no GRF cut) -- 100%" row presented as
# a result.
fs_used_grf <- isTRUE(fs$args_call_all$use_grf)

cat("\nForestSearch completed in",
    round(timings$forestsearch, 1), "seconds\n")
```


ForestSearch identifies **Estrogen ≤ 0** (ER-negative) as the subgroup with
potential harm. This is biologically plausible: tamoxifen is a selective
estrogen receptor modulator with limited efficacy in ER-negative tumors.

### Selection Diagnostic: Pareto Frontier

Beyond the single subgroup chosen by `sg_focus`, it is often informative to
inspect the *Pareto frontier* on (effect, N) -- the set of candidate subgroups
that are not dominated on both axes simultaneously. A candidate is
dominated when another candidate has at least as large an effect *and*
at least as large a sample size, with at least one strict inequality.
The frontier is a post-hoc diagnostic that lists genuine trade-off
alternatives to the selected subgroup; it does **not** affect selection.

For `"hrMinSG"` the selected subgroup may not appear on the frontier --
that focus deliberately prefers small subgroups, which can be N-dominated
by their larger neighbors.

```{r fs-pareto}
# Formatted gt table; selected subgroup is highlighted and marked with ★.
# Works uniformly for survival (HR) and GLM (OR, RR, IRR, RD, IRD, MD)
# outcomes -- effect column label and scale derived from fs$effect_measure.
pareto_frontier_table(fs)
```

```{r fs-pareto-data, eval = FALSE}
# Programmatic access (effect on natural scale, plus is_selected flag):
pareto_frontier_table(fs, format = "data.table")
```

### Agreement with GRF

ForestSearch and GRF identify subgroups by different mechanisms --
FS via exhaustive search with consistency filtering, GRF via causal
survival forests plus policy trees -- so agreement on subject-level
membership provides an informal robustness check.  `compare_fs_subgroups()`
produces a publication-ready cross-tabulation plus Cohen's kappa; it
accepts forestsearch and GRF result objects directly, and handles
non-detection (method identifies no subgroup) by assigning all
subjects to the complement.

```{r fs-grf-concordance}
sg_compare <- compare_fs_subgroups(
  fs1               = fs,
  fs2               = grf_est,
  label1            = "ForestSearch",
  label2            = "GRF Standalone",
  id.name           = id.name,
  subgroup_notation = "harm",
  title             = "FS vs GRF: Subgroup Membership Concordance",
  subtitle          = "GBSG observed data (Cox, harm search)",
  font_size         = 13
)
sg_compare$table
```

```{r fs-grf-concordance-stats}
cat("Concordance statistics:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Agreement:       %.1f%%\n",
    100 * sg_compare$concordance$agreement))
cat(sprintf("  Cohen's kappa:   %.3f\n",
    sg_compare$concordance$kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Concordant:      %d / Discordant: %d / Total: %d\n",
    sg_compare$concordance$n_agree,
    sg_compare$concordance$n_disagree,
    sg_compare$concordance$n_total))
```


# Bootstrap Bias Correction

## Rationale

Cox model estimates from identified subgroups are **upwardly biased** due to
the selection process (subgroups are selected *because* they show extreme effects).
Bootstrap bias correction addresses this by:

1. Resampling with replacement
2. Re-running the entire ForestSearch algorithm
3. Computing bias terms from bootstrap vs. observed estimates
4. Applying infinitesimal jackknife variance estimation

## Running Bootstrap Analysis

```{r bootstrap}
#| message: false
# message: false suppresses forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()'s per-iteration
# progress and its "Low events in NEW subgroup" notes (both message(), not
# cat()).  Roughly 200 lines of console noise in a NB = 1000 run; the
# low-event condition is summarised properly in the diagnostics chunk below.

t0 <- proc.time()

fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
  # Pinned to the package default.  The fit carries mr_inference = run_mr
  # (TRUE here), and each replicate/fold call copies the fit's argument
  # list, so without this the flag is inherited and MR runs inside every
  # replicate.  Nothing downstream consumes a per-replicate MR object.
  # No-op as written.
  mr_in_replicates = FALSE,
  fs.est = fs,
  nb_boots = NB,
  show_three = FALSE,
  details = FALSE,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

plan("sequential")
timings$bootstrap <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

cat("\nBootstrap completed in",
    round(timings$bootstrap / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
```

## Bootstrap Summary and Diagnostics

```{r bootstrap-summary}
# Comprehensive summary with diagnostics
summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
  sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
  boot_results = fs_bc,
  create_plots = TRUE,
  est.scale = "hr"
)

# Display bias-corrected estimates table
summaries$table
```

## MR vs. FB

The MR is a fast multiplier-bootstrap approximation of the
bootstrap bias-correction. It reuses per-candidate Cox influence (`dfbeta`) over
the selection engine's **own** candidate family — the enumerated consistency
candidates, DINA's qualifying cuts, or GRF's DR-score frontier, depending on
`fs_subgroup_method`. Its selection-bias term is computed over that family
under multiplier draws, mirroring the same search optimism the full bootstrap
corrects — without re-running the search per resample. The subgroup reported
throughout remains the one the fit selected; nothing below re-identifies it. The table below compares
MR (computed inside the fit) against the full bootstrap from the previous
section. The naive-HR row is a scale sanity check; agreement on the de-biased
row is the MR-vs-FB validation. By default the de-biased CI uses the same
infinitesimal-jackknife variance as the full bootstrap (the `ci_method = 'ij'` default),
so the de-biased row compares both point estimate and interval like-for-like. The MR de-biases both the selected
subgroup and its complement, so both appear in the comparison and the table below.

```{r debias-MR-comparison, eval = !is.null(fs$sg.harm)}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
g <- fs$mr_inference
if (is.null(g)) {
  cat("_The MR did not run (set `run_mr <- TRUE`)._\n")
} else {
  fmt_ci <- function(e, l, u) sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", e, l, u)
  fl <- function(o, n) tryCatch(as.numeric(o[[n]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  H0  <- fl(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H0"); H0l <- fl(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H0_lower"); H0u <- fl(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H0_upper")
  H2  <- fl(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H2"); H2l <- fl(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H2_lower"); H2u <- fl(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H2_upper")

  # Complement: MR from g$complement (include_complement = TRUE), FB from
  # the bootstrap's Hc_estimates.
  cc  <- g$complement
  has_cc <- !is.null(cc) && !is.null(cc$debiased) && is.finite(cc$debiased$est)
  Hc0 <- fl(fs_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0"); Hc0l <- fl(fs_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0_lower"); Hc0u <- fl(fs_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0_upper")
  Hc2 <- fl(fs_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2"); Hc2l <- fl(fs_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2_lower"); Hc2u <- fl(fs_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2_upper")

  q  <- c("naive HR (95% CI)", "de-biased HR (95% CI)")
  mr <- c(fmt_ci(g$naive$est, g$naive$lower, g$naive$upper),
          fmt_ci(g$debiased$est, g$debiased$lower, g$debiased$upper))
  fb <- c(fmt_ci(H0, H0l, H0u), fmt_ci(H2, H2l, H2u))
  if (has_cc) {
    q  <- c(q, "complement naive HR (95% CI)", "complement de-biased HR (95% CI)")
    mr <- c(mr, fmt_ci(cc$naive$est, cc$naive$lower, cc$naive$upper),
                fmt_ci(cc$debiased$est, cc$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$upper))
    fb <- c(fb, fmt_ci(Hc0, Hc0l, Hc0u), fmt_ci(Hc2, Hc2l, Hc2u))
  }
  comp <- data.frame(quantity = q, `MR` = mr,
                     `FB` = fb, check.names = FALSE)
  cat(knitr::kable(comp, row.names = FALSE,
        caption = sprintf("Selected subgroup: %s%s", paste(fs$sg.harm, collapse = " & "),
                          if (has_cc) " (complement = remaining subjects)" else "")),
      sep = "\n"); cat("\n\n")

  # Scale cross-check: MR's naive HR and the bootstrap's naive H0 are the
  # same quantity (raw subgroup HR) computed two ways; they should agree.
  if (is.finite(H0) && is.finite(g$naive$est)) {
    scale_ok <- abs(log(g$naive$est) - log(H0)) < 1e-2
    cat(sprintf("Scale cross-check (naive MR vs bootstrap H0): **%s** (%.3f vs %.3f).\n\n",
                if (scale_ok) "PASS" else "CHECK", g$naive$est, H0))
  }

  # Family is the full enumerated space, not the screened survivors.
  n_surv <- tryCatch(nrow(fs$find.grps$out.found$hr.subgroups), error = function(e) NA_integer_)
  cat(sprintf("Candidate family: %d (full <= maxk space)%s.\n\n", g$n_family,
              if (!is.na(n_surv)) sprintf("; screened survivors = %d", n_surv) else ""))

  cat(sprintf("Selection rule replayed within multiplier draws = `%s`%s.\n\n",
              if (!is.null(g$settings$reselection)) g$settings$reselection else "?",
              if (fs_subgroup_method %in% c("dina", "grf"))
                sprintf(" (a Cox-effect proxy for the %s; native-family band = %s)",
                        if (identical(fs_subgroup_method, "dina")) "DINA tau-hat" else "GRF DR-score",
                        if (is.null(fs_family_native_nbhd)) "default (matched to effect_neighborhood)"
                        else if (fs_family_native_nbhd >= 1) "off (full family)"
                        else sprintf("%.2f", fs_family_native_nbhd))
              else " (matches the consistency search statistic)"))

  boot_s <- as.numeric(timings$bootstrap)
  cat(sprintf("Timing: FB bootstrap (%d boots) %.1f s (%.1f min); MR %.2f s",
              NB, boot_s, boot_s / 60, g$timing_seconds))
  if (is.finite(boot_s) && g$timing_seconds > 0)
    cat(sprintf(" -> **%.0fx** faster (multiplier loop only; the full bootstrap scales with `NB`, MR does not)", boot_s / g$timing_seconds))
  cat(".\n\n")

  cat(sprintf("MR `mr_harm_confirmed` = **%s** (de-biased HR %.3f %s MR %.2f); selection bias %.4f (log-HR).\n",
              fs$mr_harm_confirmed, g$debiased$est,
              if (g$settings$confirm_rule == "point") "vs" else "lower-bound vs",
              g$settings$t_confirm, g$selection_bias))
  if (!is.null(g$ci_method) && !is.null(g$debiased$se_ij))
    cat(sprintf("De-biased CI: %s (IJ SE %.3f vs robust SE %.3f, log-HR).\n",
                if (identical(g$ci_method, "ij")) "infinitesimal jackknife (FB analogue)" else "robust SE",
                g$debiased$se_ij, g$debiased$se_wald))
  if (has_cc)
    cat(sprintf("Complement (n = %d): naive HR %.3f -> de-biased %.3f (selection bias %.4f, log-HR).\n",
                cc$n, cc$naive$est, cc$debiased$est, cc$selection_bias))
}
```

```{r debias-MR-no-subgroup, eval = is.null(fs$sg.harm)}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat("_No harm subgroup was selected, so the MR comparison does not apply._\n")
```

The same bias-corrected estimates table, rebuilt from the MR object. The
descriptive columns and naive effect are the same under either correction
(inherited from the bootstrap result used as a template); the bias-corrected
column carries MR's
de-biased estimate for **both** the selected subgroup and its complement.

```{r debias-MR-table, eval = !is.null(fs$sg.harm) && !is.null(fs$mr_inference)}
mr_estimates_table(fs, boot_results = fs_bc, est.scale = "hr", digits = 2)
```

```{r grf-cuts-note, eval = fs_used_grf}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat(paste(
  "Separately from whether bootstrap identifies the *same subgroup*, we can",
  "ask what raw cut GRF itself surfaced on each resample, independent of",
  "whether the downstream consistency stage accepted it.  A dominant row",
  "here paired with a low `(no GRF cut)` rate indicates that GRF's",
  "upstream discovery is stable across resamples; a frequent",
  "`(no GRF cut)` row indicates GRF itself is the source of",
  "variability.  This distinction matters because the two failure modes",
  "call for different tuning responses -- relaxing `dmin.grf` /",
  "`frac.tau` (for \"GRF produced no cut\") vs. relaxing",
  "`pconsistency.threshold` (for \"GRF produced a cut that consistency",
  "rejected\")."), "\n")
```
