```{r bootstrap-grf-cuts, eval = fs_used_grf}
if (!is.null(summaries$subgroup_summary$grf_cut_freq)) {
  summaries$subgroup_summary$grf_cut_freq |>
    utils::head(10) |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::tab_header(
      title = gt::md("**GRF cuts across bootstrap iterations**"),
      subtitle = "Top 10 by frequency; spans all bootstraps (not just successful ones)"
    ) |>
    gt::cols_label(
      Rank    = "Rank",
      grf_cut = "GRF cuts",
      N       = "N",
      Percent = "% of bootstraps"
    ) |>
    gt::fmt_number(columns = "Percent", decimals = 2) |>
    gt::tab_options(table.font.size = gt::px(13))
}
```

### Bootstrap Distributions

```{r bootstrap-plots}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

if (!is.null(summaries$plots)) {
  summaries$plots$H_distribution + summaries$plots$Hc_distribution
}
```


# DINA-Based Subgroup Identification

DINA (Doubly-robust Identification of Non-Additive effects) screens and
selects subgroups from an influence-function representation of the
covariate-specific treatment effect, fit with cross-fitting. It plugs into
the ForestSearch workflow in three complementary ways, all configured to
mirror the main Cox analysis above: same confounders, same minimum size
(`n.min = 60`), same `sg_focus`. The harm threshold is the one thing they do
*not* inherit from the main fit -- each track sets its own in the setup chunk
(`dina_screen_hr_threshold` for (A), `fs_dina_hr_threshold` for (B) and (C)),
because DINA's model-based effect is attenuated relative to the raw Cox HR. The
resolved values are in the per-fit provenance tables below.

* **(A)** ForestSearch *using DINA for screening* -- DINA's per-covariate
  frontier contributes candidate cuts to the screening pool; the consistency
  search still performs selection.
* **(B)** *Standalone DINA* with parameters analogous to (A) -- the same
  fit's frontier (the candidates (A) screens) and its single selected
  subgroup via `dina_subgroup()`.
* **(C)** ForestSearch with `subgroup_method = "dina"` -- subgroup
  *selection* is delegated to `dina_subgroup()`, then the standard
  ForestSearch bootstrap provides the selection bias-corrected Cox estimate.

```{r dina-config}
#| code-fold: false

# Shared DINA *fit* settings (Cox / survival outcome => family mapped to "cox").
# Selection parameters (sg_focus, hr_threshold) live in the setup chunk under
# the fs_dina_* knobs so they can be tuned independently; (B) and (C) read them.
dina_seed   <- 8316951
dina_nfolds <- 2
# Harm/benefit floor on the natural-parameter (log-HR) scale for ratio measures
m_diff_dina <- log(fs_dina_hr_threshold)
```

## (A) ForestSearch Using DINA for Screening

Here ForestSearch is run exactly as in the main analysis above, but with
`use_dina = TRUE`: DINA's frontier cuts are merged into the candidate pool
alongside the GRF and LASSO cuts. `dina_args` is a flat, fully-named list;
in the screening role it supplies the DINA *fit* tuning (`seed`, `n_folds`)
and the *frontier* controls (`scope`, `max_per_covariate`, `max_subgroups`).
`scope = "wide"` casts a deliberately wide net -- the consistency stage
remains the gatekeeper. By default `dina_args$selected_only = TRUE` (matching
GRF's `return_selected_cuts_only`), so screening contributes the single cut
`dina_subgroup()` would select -- using this call's `sg_focus` /
`selection_rule` / `effect_neighborhood` / `hr.threshold`, i.e. the same cut
`subgroup_method = "dina"` (C) chooses. Set `dina_args$selected_only = FALSE`
to contribute the full frontier instead (more candidates).

```{r fs-dina-screen}
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_dina_screen <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis,
  outcome.name              = outcome.name,
  event.name                = event.name,
  treat.name                = treat.name,
  id.name                   = id.name,
  confounders.name          = confounders.name,
  potentialOutcome.name     = NULL,           # default NULL
  flag_harm.name            = NULL,           # default NULL
  df.predict                = NULL,           # default NULL
  df.test                   = NULL,           # default NULL
  is.RCT                    = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  seedit                    = 8316951,        # default 8316951
  est.scale                 = "hr",           # default "hr"
  # --- Screening engines: GRF + LASSO + DINA ------------------------------
  use_lasso                 = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  use_grf                   = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  grf_res                   = NULL,           # default NULL
  grf_cuts                  = NULL,           # default NULL
  grf_depth                 = 2,              # default 2
  dmin.grf                  = 4,              # default 0.0
  frac.tau                  = 0.80,           # default 0.8
  vi.grf.min                = -0.2,           # default -0.2
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  tune_grf                  = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  use_dina                  = TRUE,           # default FALSE
  dina_res                  = NULL,           # default NULL
  dina_cuts                 = NULL,           # default NULL
  dina_args = list(                           # default list()
    seed = dina_seed, n_folds = dina_nfolds,
    scope = "wide", max_per_covariate = 3, max_subgroups = 10,
    selected_only = dina_screen_selected_only # set in setup chunk
  ),
  # --- Candidate-cut construction -----------------------------------------
  max_n_confounders         = 1000,           # default 1000
  conf_force                = NULL,           # default NULL
  defaultcut_names          = NULL,           # default NULL
  cut_type                  = "default",      # default "default"
  exclude_cuts              = NULL,           # default NULL
  replace_med_grf           = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  cont.cutoff               = 4,              # default 4
  conf.cont_medians         = NULL,           # default NULL
  conf.cont_medians_force   = NULL,           # default NULL
  conf.cont_jcuts           = NULL,           # default NULL
  # --- Selection engine ---------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method           = "consistency",  # default "consistency"; or "dina"
  sg_focus                  = dina_screen_sg_focus,    # set in setup chunk
  selection_rule            = "neighborhood",  # default "neighborhood"
  effect_neighborhood       = 0.10,            # default 0.10
  # --- Subgroup constraints -----------------------------------------------
  n.min                     = 60,             # default 60
  d0.min                    = 10,             # default 10
  d1.min                    = 10,             # default 10
  maxk                      = 2,              # default 2
  max_subgroups_search      = dina_screen_max_subgroups_search,  # set in setup chunk
  # --- Thresholds (survival / HR scale) -----------------------------------
  hr.threshold              = dina_screen_hr_threshold,    # set in setup chunk
  hr.consistency            = dina_screen_hr_consistency,  # set in setup chunk
  effect.threshold          = NULL,           # default NULL (alias of hr.threshold)
  consistency.threshold     = NULL,           # default NULL (alias of hr.consistency)
  pconsistency.threshold    = 0.90,           # default 0.90
  consistency_method        = fs_consistency_method,  # ALIGN: match main run + ACTG175 (MR/consistency parity)
  m1.threshold              = Inf,            # default Inf
  minp                      = 0.025,          # default 0.025
  # --- Consistency search -------------------------------------------------
  fs.splits                 = 1000,           # default 1000
  stop_threshold            = NULL,           # NULL is what this configuration RESOLVES to, not a
                                              #   preference.  This call's sg_focus ("effMaxSG")
                                              #   normalizes to "hrMaxSG", and forestsearch_main.R:1403
                                              #   resets stop_threshold to NULL for that focus: a
                                              #   neighborhood band needs every candidate evaluated,
                                              #   so a truncated scan is unsound.  Any non-NULL value
                                              #   reaches the same NULL but warns on every render;
                                              #   passing NULL skips the reset branch outright (its
                                              #   guard is !is.null(stop_threshold)).  Named here so
                                              #   the resolved setting stays inspectable.
  use_twostage              = TRUE,           # default TRUE
  twostage_args             = list(),         # default list()
  max.minutes               = 3,              # default 3
  # --- Output / diagnostics -----------------------------------------------
  show_candidate_summary    = TRUE,           # default FALSE
  details                   = TRUE,           # default FALSE
  quiet                     = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  by.risk                   = 12,             # default 12
  plot.sg                   = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  plot.grf                  = FALSE,          # default FALSE
  # --- Parallel -----------------------------------------------------------
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

plan("sequential")
timings$fs_dina_screen <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
stopifnot(!is.null(fs_dina_screen), !is.null(fs_dina_screen$args_call_all))

cat("Identified subgroup (H):",
    paste(fs_dina_screen$sg.harm, collapse = " & "), "\n")
cat("Subgroup size:", sum(fs_dina_screen$df.est$treat.recommend == 0),
    sprintf("(%.1f%% of ITT)\n",
            100 * mean(fs_dina_screen$df.est$treat.recommend == 0)))
```

```{r fs-dina-screen-param-provenance}
#| echo: false
fs_param_table(fs_dina_screen, "(A) DINA-screened fit: resolved parameters")
```

The cuts DINA contributed to the candidate pool are recorded on the result
object. These are exactly the frontier candidates reproduced standalone in
(B).

```{r fs-dina-screen-cuts}
dina_screen_cuts <- fs_dina_screen$dina_cuts
if (length(dina_screen_cuts) > 0) {
  gt(data.frame(
    `#` = seq_along(dina_screen_cuts),
    `DINA candidate cut` = dina_screen_cuts,
    check.names = FALSE
  )) |>
    tab_header(title = "DINA Screening Candidates Injected into ForestSearch") |>
    cols_align(align = "left")
} else {
  cat("DINA contributed no candidate cuts under the configured frontier.\n")
}
```

```{r fs-dina-screen-pareto}
# Selection diagnostic for the DINA-screened run (selected subgroup marked).
pareto_frontier_table(fs_dina_screen)
```

## (B) Standalone DINA

The same DINA fit, run outside ForestSearch. Its `dina_frontier()` output is
the candidate set fed into screening in (A); its `dina_subgroup()` output is
the single subgroup selected by DINA itself -- the mechanism (C) uses
internally. Parameters are analogous to (A): same confounders, `n_min = 60`,
and `sg_focus`, with the harm floor `m_diff = log(fs_dina_hr_threshold)` set in
the dina-config chunk below (so (B) and (C) share one floor by construction).

```{r dina-standalone-fit}
t0 <- proc.time()

dina_fit <- dina(
  df         = df.analysis,
  outcome    = outcome.name,
  treatment  = treat.name,
  covariates = confounders.name,
  family     = "cox",          # default "gaussian"; gaussian/binomial/poisson/cox
  status     = event.name,     # default NULL (required for family = "cox")
  # ... forwarded to dina_fit():
  seed              = dina_seed,   # default NULL
  n_folds           = dina_nfolds, # default 2L
  propensity_method = "logistic",  # default "logistic"
  baseline_method   = NULL,        # default NULL
  cross_fitting     = TRUE,        # default TRUE
  cens_type         = NULL,        # default NULL (no censoring model)
  cens_params       = list(),      # default list()
  n_grid            = 500L,        # default 500L
  eps               = 1e-6         # default 1e-6
)

timings$dina_standalone <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
cat("Standalone DINA fit complete (family = cox).\n")
```

### DINA Frontier (Screening Candidates)

```{r dina-standalone-frontier}
dina_fr <- dina_frontier(
  fit               = dina_fit,
  df                = df.analysis,
  covariates        = confounders.name,
  scope             = "wide",     # default "wide"; or "harm" (requires m_diff)
  m_diff            = NULL,        # default NULL (no effect floor under scope = "wide")
  n_min             = 60,         # default 60L
  direction         = "both",     # default "both"; or "left" / "right"
  max_per_covariate = 3,          # default 3L
  max_subgroups     = 10,         # default 10L
  digits            = 3           # default 3L
)

gt(dina_fr[, c("covariate", "direction", "threshold",
               "n_subgroup", "effect", "cut_expr")]) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Standalone DINA Frontier",
    subtitle = "Per-covariate non-dominated (effect, N) candidates; effect on HR scale"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(threshold, effect), decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(
    covariate = "Covariate", direction = "Direction",
    threshold = "Threshold", n_subgroup = "N", effect = "HR",
    cut_expr = "Cut"
  ) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = c(covariate, direction, cut_expr))
```

### DINA-Selected Subgroup

```{r dina-standalone-select}
dina_sel <- dina_subgroup(
  fit                 = dina_fit,
  df                  = df.analysis,
  covariates          = confounders.name,
  m_diff              = m_diff_dina,
  n_min               = 60,             # default 60L
  direction           = "both",         # default "both"; or "left" / "right"
  sg_focus            = fs_dina_sg_focus,  # set in setup chunk
  selection_rule      = "neighborhood",  # default "neighborhood"; pareto/both (hrMaxSG/hrMinSG)
  effect_neighborhood = 0.10,            # default 0.10
  alpha               = 0.05             # default 0.05
)

if (isTRUE(dina_sel$found)) {
  op <- if (identical(dina_sel$direction, "left")) "<=" else ">="
  cat(sprintf("DINA-selected subgroup: %s %s %s\n",
              dina_sel$covariate, op, format(dina_sel$threshold)))
  cat(sprintf("Direction: %s | N = %d\n",
              dina_sel$direction, dina_sel$n_subgroup))
} else {
  cat("Standalone DINA selected no subgroup meeting the criteria.\n")
}
```

## (C) ForestSearch with `subgroup_method = "dina"`

In this mode ForestSearch delegates subgroup *selection* to
`dina_subgroup()`, bypassing GRF, LASSO and the consistency search. The
selection criteria are inherited from this call's `sg_focus`, `n.min` and
`hr.threshold` (mapped to the log-HR harm floor); `dina_args` supplies only
the fit tuning. The returned object is a standard `forestsearch` result, so
the existing bootstrap machinery applies unchanged.

```{r fs-dina-select}
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_dina <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis,
  outcome.name        = outcome.name,
  event.name          = event.name,
  treat.name          = treat.name,
  id.name             = id.name,
  confounders.name    = confounders.name,
  df.predict          = NULL,            # default NULL
  df.test             = NULL,            # default NULL
  is.RCT              = TRUE,            # default TRUE
  seedit              = 8316951,         # default 8316951
  # --- DINA-selection mode ------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method     = "dina",          # default "consistency"
  dina_args           = list(seed = dina_seed, n_folds = dina_nfolds),  # fit tuning only
  dina_select_statistic = fs_dina_select_statistic,  # setup-chunk selector (top-level)
  dina_res            = NULL,            # default NULL (reuse a fitted dina object)
  # --- Selection criteria (passed through to dina_subgroup) ---------------
  sg_focus            = fs_dina_sg_focus,  # set in setup chunk
  selection_rule      = "neighborhood",  # default "neighborhood"
  effect_neighborhood = 0.10,            # default 0.10
  n.min               = 60,              # default 60
  hr.threshold        = fs_dina_hr_threshold,  # set in setup chunk (-> log-HR floor)
  # --- MR ----------------------------------------------
  mr_inference         = run_mr,           # set in setup chunk
  mr_inference_args    = list(draws = mr_draws,
                             family_native_neighborhood = fs_dina_family_native_nbhd),
  # --- Output -------------------------------------------------------------
  details             = TRUE             # default FALSE
  # NOTE: subgroup_method = "dina" bypasses GRF, LASSO and the consistency
  # search; use_grf / use_lasso / use_twostage / fs.splits / maxk /
  # stop_threshold and related parameters do not apply in this mode.
)

timings$fs_dina_select <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
stopifnot(!is.null(fs_dina), !is.null(fs_dina$args_call_all))

cat("DINA-selected subgroup (H):",
    paste(fs_dina$sg.harm, collapse = " & "), "\n")
cat("Subgroup size:", sum(fs_dina$df.est$treat.recommend == 0),
    sprintf("(%.1f%% of ITT)\n",
            100 * mean(fs_dina$df.est$treat.recommend == 0)))
```

```{r fs-dina-param-provenance}
#| echo: false
fs_param_table(fs_dina, "(C) subgroup_method = dina: resolved parameters")
```

Under `subgroup_method = "dina"` the consistency search, LASSO and GRF screens
are bypassed. The table still lists every formal, so the inert ones appear as
resolved defaults rather than silently absent.

### Bootstrap Bias-Corrected Cox Estimates

The within-subgroup Cox hazard ratio is upwardly biased by selection. The
ForestSearch bootstrap corrects this by re-running the full pipeline on each
resample; because the result above was produced in DINA-selection mode, each
replicate re-fits DINA and re-runs `dina_subgroup()` from scratch -- so the
correction reflects the DINA selection process itself.

```{r fs-dina-bootstrap, eval = !is.null(fs_dina$sg.harm)}
#| message: false
# message: false suppresses forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()'s per-iteration
# progress and its "Low events in NEW subgroup" notes (both message(), not
# cat()).  Roughly 200 lines of console noise in a NB = 1000 run; the
# low-event condition is summarised properly in the diagnostics chunk below.
# Runs only when DINA identified a subgroup.  The bootstrap bias-corrects an
# identified subgroup's effect, so there is nothing to do otherwise.
t0 <- proc.time()

# details = TRUE keeps per-iteration output visible while validating DINA-mode
# bootstrap.  The plan is "multisession" (production speed); switch it to
# "sequential" if errors need to surface in loop order.

fs_dina_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
  # Pinned to the package default, as at the main bootstrap above -- see the
  # comment there for why this is a no-op.
  mr_in_replicates = FALSE,
  fs.est = fs_dina,
  nb_boots = NB,
  show_three = FALSE,
  details = TRUE,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

plan("sequential")
timings$fs_dina_bootstrap <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

cat("\nDINA-mode bootstrap completed in",
    round(timings$fs_dina_bootstrap / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
```

```{r fs-dina-no-subgroup, eval = is.null(fs_dina$sg.harm)}
# Shown only when DINA selected no subgroup at the configured harm floor.
timings$fs_dina_bootstrap <- 0
cat("DINA (subgroup_method = \"dina\") identified no subgroup at",
    "hr.threshold =", fs_dina_hr_threshold, "-- bootstrap skipped.\n",
    "DINA's model-based effect is attenuated relative to the raw Cox HR,",
    "so this floor may not be reached; see the standalone DINA frontier (B)",
    "for the achievable effect range, and lower the DINA harm floor if a",
    "bootstrap demonstration is desired.\n")
```

```{r fs-dina-bootstrap-summary, eval = !is.null(fs_dina$sg.harm)}
dina_summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
  sgharm = fs_dina$sg.harm,
  boot_results = fs_dina_bc,
  create_plots = FALSE,
  est.scale = "hr"
)

dina_summaries$table
```

#### MR (counterpart to FB)

The same MR-vs-FB comparison as the main analysis, for the
DINA-selection fit. The MR de-biases against DINA's **own** qualifying
candidate family (re-running nothing), while the bootstrap above re-runs DINA on
every resample.

For DINA, FB and MR are **not** expected to agree as tightly as for the
consistency method. DINA selects on its survival-forest **tau-hat**, but MR's de-biasing is
computed on the perturbed **Cox** effect; over a large depth-2 candidate family
the winner's-curse term can therefore exceed the bootstrap's and over-correct
the selected subgroup. To keep that band close to DINA's own selection band,
MR by default restricts its family to
candidates competitive on DINA's native tau-hat, matching the band to
`effect_neighborhood` (the recommended default, used here via
`fs_dina_family_native_nbhd <- NULL`; set an explicit number for a different band,
or `>= 1` to de-bias against the full unrestricted family). The complement is the
induced residual rather than a max-over-family selection, so FB and MR agree on
it regardless. This band tunes only the *candidate-competition* part of the
bias -- MR holds the survival forest fixed, so the forest-refit optimism is
invisible to it; treat the full bootstrap as the reference for DINA and MR
as a fast, conservative check.

```{r fs-dina-debias-MR-comparison, eval = !is.null(fs_dina$sg.harm)}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
g <- fs_dina$mr_inference
if (is.null(g)) {
  cat("_The MR did not run (set `run_mr <- TRUE`)._\n")
} else {
  fmt_ci <- function(e, l, u) sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", e, l, u)
  fl <- function(o, n) tryCatch(as.numeric(o[[n]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  H0 <- fl(fs_dina_bc$H_estimates, "H0"); H0l <- fl(fs_dina_bc$H_estimates, "H0_lower"); H0u <- fl(fs_dina_bc$H_estimates, "H0_upper")
  H2 <- fl(fs_dina_bc$H_estimates, "H2"); H2l <- fl(fs_dina_bc$H_estimates, "H2_lower"); H2u <- fl(fs_dina_bc$H_estimates, "H2_upper")
  cc <- g$complement
  has_cc <- !is.null(cc) && !is.null(cc$debiased) && is.finite(cc$debiased$est)
  q  <- c("naive HR (95% CI)", "de-biased HR (95% CI)")
  mr <- c(fmt_ci(g$naive$est, g$naive$lower, g$naive$upper),
          fmt_ci(g$debiased$est, g$debiased$lower, g$debiased$upper))
  fb <- c(fmt_ci(H0, H0l, H0u), fmt_ci(H2, H2l, H2u))
  if (has_cc) {
    Hc0 <- fl(fs_dina_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0"); Hc0l <- fl(fs_dina_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0_lower"); Hc0u <- fl(fs_dina_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0_upper")
    Hc2 <- fl(fs_dina_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2"); Hc2l <- fl(fs_dina_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2_lower"); Hc2u <- fl(fs_dina_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2_upper")
    q  <- c(q, "complement naive HR (95% CI)", "complement de-biased HR (95% CI)")
    mr <- c(mr, fmt_ci(cc$naive$est, cc$naive$lower, cc$naive$upper),
                fmt_ci(cc$debiased$est, cc$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$upper))
    fb <- c(fb, fmt_ci(Hc0, Hc0l, Hc0u), fmt_ci(Hc2, Hc2l, Hc2u))
  }
  comp <- data.frame(quantity = q, `MR` = mr,
                     `FB` = fb, check.names = FALSE)
  cat(knitr::kable(comp, row.names = FALSE,
        caption = sprintf("DINA-selected subgroup: %s%s",
                          paste(fs_dina$sg.harm, collapse = " & "),
                          if (has_cc) " (complement = remaining subjects)" else "")),
      sep = "\n"); cat("\n\n")

  boot_s <- as.numeric(timings$fs_dina_bootstrap)
  cat(sprintf("Timing: FB bootstrap (%d boots) %.1f s (%.1f min); MR %.2f s",
              NB, boot_s, boot_s / 60, g$timing_seconds))
  if (is.finite(boot_s) && g$timing_seconds > 0)
    cat(sprintf(" -> **%.0fx** faster (the bootstrap scales with `NB`, MR does not)",
                boot_s / g$timing_seconds))
  cat(".\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("MR harm flag = **%s** (de-biased HR %.3f %s MR %.2f); selection bias %.4f (log-HR); candidate family = %d.\n",
              isTRUE(g$harm_flag), g$debiased$est,
              if (g$settings$confirm_rule == "point") "vs" else "lower-bound vs",
              g$settings$t_confirm, g$selection_bias, g$n_family))
  cat(sprintf("Selection rule replayed within multiplier draws = `%s` (a Cox-effect proxy for DINA's tau-hat); native-family band = %s.\n",
              if (!is.null(g$settings$reselection)) g$settings$reselection else "?",
              if (is.null(fs_dina_family_native_nbhd)) "default (matched to effect_neighborhood)"
              else if (fs_dina_family_native_nbhd >= 1) "off (full family)"
              else sprintf("%.2f (restricted to tau-hat-competitive candidates)",
                           fs_dina_family_native_nbhd)))
  if (!is.null(g$ci_method) && !is.null(g$debiased$se_ij))
    cat(sprintf("De-biased CI: %s (IJ SE %.3f vs robust SE %.3f, log-HR).\n",
                if (identical(g$ci_method, "ij")) "infinitesimal jackknife (FB analogue)" else "robust SE",
                g$debiased$se_ij, g$debiased$se_wald))
}
```

The FB bias-corrected table above, rebuilt from the MR object (the
descriptive columns and naive effect are the same under either correction; the
bias-corrected column carries MR's de-biased estimate for the subgroup and its
complement).

```{r fs-dina-debias-MR-table, eval = !is.null(fs_dina$sg.harm) && !is.null(fs_dina$mr_inference)}
mr_estimates_table(fs_dina, boot_results = fs_dina_bc, est.scale = "hr", digits = 2)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Screening vs. selection roles for DINA

`dina_args` behaves differently by role. In the **screening** path (A,
`use_dina = TRUE`) it defaults to `selected_only = TRUE` (matching GRF's
`return_selected_cuts_only`): the screening path calls `dina_subgroup()` and
contributes only its selected cut, so it *does* consult this call's
`sg_focus` / `selection_rule` / `effect_neighborhood` -- yielding the same
cut the selection path (C) would choose. Setting `selected_only = FALSE`
instead drives `dina_frontier()`, which is selection-agnostic (`sg_focus` /
`selection_rule` are *not* consulted) and contributes the full candidate set.
In the **selection** path (C, `subgroup_method = "dina"`) the selection is
always driven by this call's `sg_focus` / `selection_rule` /
`effect_neighborhood` via `dina_subgroup()`, and `dina_args` supplies only
the fit. This mode is currently depth-1 (a
single covariate threshold).
:::



## (D) ForestSearch with `subgroup_method = "grf"`

In this mode ForestSearch delegates subgroup *selection* to GRF -- a causal-forest
policy tree (`grf_selection = "tree"`) or the doubly-robust-score frontier
(`"frontier"`) -- bypassing LASSO, DINA and the consistency search. The selection
criteria are inherited from this call's `sg_focus` (mapped to the GRF frontier/tree
rule), `n.min`, `grf_depth`, `grf_selection` and the DR-score harm floor
`dmin.grf`. The returned object is a standard `forestsearch` result, so the
existing bootstrap machinery applies unchanged.

```{r fs-grf-select}
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_grf <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis,
  outcome.name        = outcome.name,
  event.name          = event.name,
  treat.name          = treat.name,
  id.name             = id.name,
  confounders.name    = confounders.name,
  df.predict          = NULL,            # default NULL
  df.test             = NULL,            # default NULL
  is.RCT              = TRUE,            # default TRUE
  seedit              = 8316951,         # default 8316951 (also seeds the forest)
  # --- GRF-selection mode -------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method     = "grf",           # default "consistency"
  grf_selection       = fs_grf_demo_selection,  # set in setup chunk ("tree" | "frontier")
  grf_select_statistic = fs_grf_select_statistic,  # set in setup chunk (frontier only)
  grf_depth           = fs_grf_demo_depth,      # set in setup chunk (tree / DR-pair depth)
  dmin.grf            = fs_grf_demo_dmin,        # set in setup chunk (DR-score harm floor)
  frac.tau            = 0.8,             # default 0.8 (RMST truncation fraction)
  grf_res             = NULL,            # default NULL (reuse a fitted forest)
  # --- Selection criteria -------------------------------------------------
  sg_focus            = fs_grf_sg_focus,  # set in setup chunk (-> GRF frontier/tree rule)
  selection_rule      = "neighborhood",  # default "neighborhood"
  effect_neighborhood = 0.10,            # default 0.10
  n.min               = 60,              # default 60
  # --- MR ----------------------------------------------
  mr_inference         = run_mr,           # set in setup chunk
  mr_inference_args    = list(draws = mr_draws,
                             family_native_neighborhood = fs_grf_family_native_nbhd),
  # --- Output -------------------------------------------------------------
  details             = TRUE             # default FALSE
  # NOTE: subgroup_method = "grf" bypasses LASSO, DINA and the consistency
  # search; use_lasso / use_dina / use_twostage / fs.splits / maxk /
  # hr.threshold / pconsistency.threshold do not apply in this mode.
)

timings$fs_grf_select <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
stopifnot(!is.null(fs_grf), !is.null(fs_grf$args_call_all))

cat("GRF-selected subgroup (H):",
    paste(fs_grf$sg.harm, collapse = " & "), "\n")
cat("Subgroup size:", sum(fs_grf$df.est$treat.recommend == 0),
    sprintf("(%.1f%% of ITT)\n",
            100 * mean(fs_grf$df.est$treat.recommend == 0)))
```

```{r fs-grf-param-provenance}
#| echo: false
fs_param_table(fs_grf, "(D) subgroup_method = grf: resolved parameters")
```

### Bootstrap Bias-Corrected Cox Estimates

The within-subgroup Cox hazard ratio is upwardly biased by selection. The
ForestSearch bootstrap corrects this by re-running the full pipeline on each
resample; because the result above was produced in GRF-selection mode, each
replicate re-fits the causal forest and re-runs GRF selection from scratch -- so
the correction reflects the GRF selection process itself.

```{r fs-grf-bootstrap, eval = !is.null(fs_grf$sg.harm)}
#| message: false
# message: false suppresses forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()'s per-iteration
# progress and its "Low events in NEW subgroup" notes (both message(), not
# cat()).  Roughly 200 lines of console noise in a NB = 1000 run; the
# low-event condition is summarised properly in the diagnostics chunk below.
# Runs only when GRF identified a subgroup.  The bootstrap bias-corrects an
# identified subgroup's effect, so there is nothing to do otherwise.
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_grf_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
  # Pinned to the package default, as at the main bootstrap above -- see the
  # comment there for why this is a no-op.
  mr_in_replicates = FALSE,
  fs.est = fs_grf,
  nb_boots = NB,
  show_three = FALSE,
  details = TRUE,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

plan("sequential")
timings$fs_grf_bootstrap <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

cat("\nGRF-mode bootstrap completed in",
    round(timings$fs_grf_bootstrap / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
```

```{r fs-grf-no-subgroup, eval = is.null(fs_grf$sg.harm)}
# Shown only when GRF selected no subgroup at the configured DR-score floor.
timings$fs_grf_bootstrap <- 0
cat("GRF (subgroup_method = \"grf\") identified no subgroup at",
    "dmin.grf =", fs_grf_demo_dmin, "-- bootstrap skipped.\n",
    "Lower the DR-score floor (dmin.grf) or switch grf_selection /",
    "grf_depth if a bootstrap demonstration is desired.\n")
```

```{r fs-grf-bootstrap-summary, eval = !is.null(fs_grf$sg.harm)}
grf_summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
  sgharm = fs_grf$sg.harm,
  boot_results = fs_grf_bc,
  create_plots = FALSE,
  est.scale = "hr"
)

grf_summaries$table
```

#### MR (counterpart to FB)

The same MR-vs-FB comparison as the main analysis, for the
GRF-selection fit. The MR de-biases against GRF's **own** DR-score candidate
family (re-running nothing), while the bootstrap above re-runs GRF on every
resample.

As with DINA, FB and MR are **not** expected to agree as tightly as for the
consistency method. GRF selects on its **doubly-robust (RMST-based) score**, but
MR's de-biasing is computed on the perturbed **Cox** effect; the additive RMST
scale and the multiplicative hazard scale need not rank candidates the same way,
so over a large candidate family the winner's-curse term can exceed the
bootstrap's and over-correct the selected subgroup. To keep that band close to
GRF's own selection band, MR by default restricts its family to candidates competitive on GRF's native DR-score, matching
the band to `effect_neighborhood` (the recommended default, used here via
`fs_grf_family_native_nbhd <- NULL`; set an explicit number for a different band,
or `>= 1` to de-bias against the full family). The complement is the induced
residual rather than a max-over-family selection, so FB and MR agree on it
regardless. Two caveats specific to GRF: a *dominant* DR-score winner can collapse
the restricted family to a single candidate (`candidate family = 1` in the note
below), in which case MR removes only MR-threshold optimism; and,
more fundamentally, the band tunes only the *candidate-competition* part of the
bias -- MR holds the causal forest fixed, so the forest-refit optimism that
the bootstrap captures is invisible to it. Treat the full bootstrap as the
reference for GRF and MR as a fast, conservative check.

```{r fs-grf-debias-MR-comparison, eval = !is.null(fs_grf$sg.harm)}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
g <- fs_grf$mr_inference
if (is.null(g)) {
  cat("_The MR did not run (set `run_mr <- TRUE`)._\n")
} else {
  fmt_ci <- function(e, l, u) sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", e, l, u)
  fl <- function(o, n) tryCatch(as.numeric(o[[n]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  H0 <- fl(fs_grf_bc$H_estimates, "H0"); H0l <- fl(fs_grf_bc$H_estimates, "H0_lower"); H0u <- fl(fs_grf_bc$H_estimates, "H0_upper")
  H2 <- fl(fs_grf_bc$H_estimates, "H2"); H2l <- fl(fs_grf_bc$H_estimates, "H2_lower"); H2u <- fl(fs_grf_bc$H_estimates, "H2_upper")
  cc <- g$complement
  has_cc <- !is.null(cc) && !is.null(cc$debiased) && is.finite(cc$debiased$est)
  q  <- c("naive HR (95% CI)", "de-biased HR (95% CI)")
  mr <- c(fmt_ci(g$naive$est, g$naive$lower, g$naive$upper),
          fmt_ci(g$debiased$est, g$debiased$lower, g$debiased$upper))
  fb <- c(fmt_ci(H0, H0l, H0u), fmt_ci(H2, H2l, H2u))
  if (has_cc) {
    Hc0 <- fl(fs_grf_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0"); Hc0l <- fl(fs_grf_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0_lower"); Hc0u <- fl(fs_grf_bc$Hc_estimates, "H0_upper")
    Hc2 <- fl(fs_grf_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2"); Hc2l <- fl(fs_grf_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2_lower"); Hc2u <- fl(fs_grf_bc$Hc_estimates, "H2_upper")
    q  <- c(q, "complement naive HR (95% CI)", "complement de-biased HR (95% CI)")
    mr <- c(mr, fmt_ci(cc$naive$est, cc$naive$lower, cc$naive$upper),
                fmt_ci(cc$debiased$est, cc$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$upper))
    fb <- c(fb, fmt_ci(Hc0, Hc0l, Hc0u), fmt_ci(Hc2, Hc2l, Hc2u))
  }
  comp <- data.frame(quantity = q, `MR` = mr,
                     `FB` = fb, check.names = FALSE)
  cat(knitr::kable(comp, row.names = FALSE,
        caption = sprintf("GRF-selected subgroup: %s%s",
                          paste(fs_grf$sg.harm, collapse = " & "),
                          if (has_cc) " (complement = remaining subjects)" else "")),
      sep = "\n"); cat("\n\n")

  boot_s <- as.numeric(timings$fs_grf_bootstrap)
  cat(sprintf("Timing: FB bootstrap (%d boots) %.1f s (%.1f min); MR %.2f s",
              NB, boot_s, boot_s / 60, g$timing_seconds))
  if (is.finite(boot_s) && g$timing_seconds > 0)
    cat(sprintf(" -> **%.0fx** faster (the bootstrap scales with `NB`, MR does not)",
                boot_s / g$timing_seconds))
  cat(".\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("MR harm flag = **%s** (de-biased HR %.3f %s MR %.2f); selection bias %.4f (log-HR); candidate family = %d.\n",
              isTRUE(g$harm_flag), g$debiased$est,
              if (g$settings$confirm_rule == "point") "vs" else "lower-bound vs",
              g$settings$t_confirm, g$selection_bias, g$n_family))
  cat(sprintf("Selection rule replayed within multiplier draws = `%s` (a Cox-effect proxy for GRF's DR-score); native-family band = %s.\n",
              if (!is.null(g$settings$reselection)) g$settings$reselection else "?",
              if (is.null(fs_grf_family_native_nbhd)) "default (matched to effect_neighborhood)"
              else if (fs_grf_family_native_nbhd >= 1) "off (full family)"
              else sprintf("%.2f (restricted to DR-score-competitive candidates)",
                           fs_grf_family_native_nbhd)))
  if (!is.null(g$ci_method) && !is.null(g$debiased$se_ij))
    cat(sprintf("De-biased CI: %s (IJ SE %.3f vs robust SE %.3f, log-HR).\n",
                if (identical(g$ci_method, "ij")) "infinitesimal jackknife (FB analogue)" else "robust SE",
                g$debiased$se_ij, g$debiased$se_wald))
}
```

The FB bias-corrected table above, rebuilt from the MR object (the
descriptive columns and naive effect are the same under either correction; the
bias-corrected column carries MR's de-biased estimate for the subgroup and its
complement).

```{r fs-grf-debias-MR-table, eval = !is.null(fs_grf$sg.harm) && !is.null(fs_grf$mr_inference)}
mr_estimates_table(fs_grf, boot_results = fs_grf_bc, est.scale = "hr", digits = 2)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Selection statistic vs. MR's de-biasing scale (GRF)

GRF ranks candidates by the **doubly-robust score** (RMST-based for survival),
while MR's de-biasing is computed on the perturbed **Cox** effect. The two scales
(additive RMST vs. multiplicative hazard) need not agree, so MR is a
*proxy* for GRF's selection -- the same approximation noted for DINA's tau-hat.
`family_native_neighborhood` restricts MR family to DR-score-competitive
candidates to keep that proxy close to GRF's actual selection neighbourhood; the
full bootstrap remains the reference because it re-runs the DR-score selection
itself.
:::



# Cross-Validation

Cross-validation assesses the **stability** of the ForestSearch algorithm.
Two approaches are available:

## K-Fold Cross-Validation

```{r cv-skipped-note, eval = !run_cv}
cat("K-Fold cross-validation skipped (run_cv = FALSE). Set run_cv <- TRUE",
    "in the parallel-setup chunk to run it.\n")
```

```{r kfold-cv, eval = run_cv}

t0 <- proc.time()

fs_kfold <- forestsearch_tenfold(
  # Pinned to the package default.  The fit carries mr_inference = run_mr
  # (TRUE here), and each replicate/fold call copies the fit's argument
  # list, so without this the flag is inherited and MR runs inside every
  # replicate.  Nothing downstream consumes a per-replicate MR object.
  # No-op as written.
  mr_in_replicates = FALSE,
  fs.est = fs,
  sims = Ksims,
  Kfolds = Kfolds_cv,
  details = FALSE,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = FALSE
  )
)

plan("sequential")
timings$kfold <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
metrics_tables <- cv_metrics_tables(fs_kfold)
metrics_tables
```

# Summary and Interpretation

## Key Findings

```{r summary-findings}
cat(strrep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("FORESTSEARCH ANALYSIS SUMMARY\n")
cat(strrep("=", 60), "\n\n")

cat("Dataset: GBSG (N =", nrow(df.analysis), ")\n")
cat("Outcome: Recurrence-free survival\n\n")

cat("ITT Analysis:\n")
cat("  HR (95% CI): 0.69 (0.54, 0.89)\n\n")

cat("Identified Subgroup (H):\n")
cat("  Definition:", paste(fs$sg.harm, collapse = " & "), "\n")
cat("  Size:", sum(fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 0),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 0)))
cat("  Unadjusted HR:",
    sprintf("%.2f", exp(fs$grp.consistency$out_sg$result$hr[1])), "\n")

cat("\nComplement Subgroup (Hc):\n")
cat("  Size:", sum(fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 1),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 1)))
```

## Clinical Interpretation

The ForestSearch analysis identifies **estrogen receptor-negative (ER ≤ 0)**
patients as a subgroup with potential lack of benefit from hormonal therapy.

**Biological plausibility**: Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor
modulator. Its efficacy depends on ER expression. The finding that ER-negative
patients may not benefit is consistent with:

- Mechanistic understanding of tamoxifen action
- Meta-analyses showing no tamoxifen benefit in ER-negative breast cancer
- Clinical guidelines recommending tamoxifen primarily for ER-positive tumors

**Caveats**:

1. This is an **exploratory** analysis requiring independent validation
2. The bias-corrected estimates have wider confidence intervals
3. Cross-validation metrics should be evaluated for algorithm stability

## Computational Timing

```{r timing-summary}
timings$total <- (proc.time() - t_vignette_start)["elapsed"]

# The rows are DRIVEN BY names(timings), not typed out.  A hand-written row list
# is how the (D) GRF fit and its bootstrap went missing from this table while
# still counting toward Total.  This map supplies readable labels and the
# display order; anything timed above but not labelled here STOPS the render
# rather than being silently dropped.
.timing_labels <- c(
  grf               = "GRF (preliminary)",
  forestsearch      = "ForestSearch (main fit)",
  bootstrap         = "FB bootstrap (main)",
  fs_dina_screen    = "FS (DINA screening)",
  dina_standalone   = "DINA (standalone)",
  fs_dina_select    = "FS (subgroup_method=dina)",
  fs_dina_bootstrap = "FB bootstrap (DINA)",
  fs_grf_select     = "FS (subgroup_method=grf)",
  fs_grf_bootstrap  = "FB bootstrap (GRF)",
  kfold             = "K-fold CV",
  oob               = "Leave-one-out CV",
  total             = "Total"
)

.unlabelled <- setdiff(names(timings), names(.timing_labels))
if (length(.unlabelled))
  stop("Computational Timing: no label for timings$",
       paste(.unlabelled, collapse = ", timings$"),
       " -- add it to .timing_labels in the timing-summary chunk.")

# Display order follows the map; Total last.  Skipped analyses (run_cv /
# run_loo FALSE) are pre-seeded NA and still get a row, so the reader sees
# that they were skipped rather than that they were forgotten.
.ord <- intersect(names(.timing_labels), names(timings))
.ord <- c(setdiff(.ord, "total"), intersect("total", .ord))

timing_df <- data.frame(
  Analysis  = unname(.timing_labels[.ord]),
  Seconds   = vapply(.ord, function(k) as.numeric(timings[[k]]), numeric(1)),
  row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
timing_df$Minutes <- timing_df$Seconds / 60

# Reconciliation: Total is the whole-document wall clock, so it legitimately
# exceeds the sum of the timed blocks (data prep, tables, figures, rendering are
# not timed).  Stating the residual makes an unexplained gap visible.
.parts_s <- sum(timing_df$Seconds[.ord != "total"], na.rm = TRUE)
.total_s <- as.numeric(timings$total)
.resid_s <- .total_s - .parts_s

gt(timing_df) |>
  tab_header(title = "Computational Timing") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(Seconds, Minutes), decimals = 1) |>
  cols_label(
    Analysis = "Component",
    Seconds = "Time (sec)",
    Minutes = "Time (min)"
  ) |>
  tab_footnote(footnote = md(sprintf(
    paste("Rows are generated from `names(timings)`; a timed component with no",
          "label stops the render. Timed blocks account for %.1f s of the %.1f s",
          "total, leaving %.1f s (%.0f%%) in untimed work (data prep, tables,",
          "figures, document rendering). `NA` marks an analysis a toggle skipped."),
    .parts_s, .total_s, .resid_s, 100 * .resid_s / .total_s)))
```

# Parameter provenance (all fits) {#sec-param-appendix}

Formals whose resolved value differs from the package default, stacked across
the four fits. Values are read from each fit's `args_call_all`, so this table
cannot drift from the code that produced the results.

```{r param-provenance-appendix}
#| echo: false
.fits <- list("FS (main)" = fs, "(A) DINA-screened" = fs_dina_screen,
              "(C) DINA-selected" = fs_dina, "(D) GRF-selected" = fs_grf)
.pp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(.fits), function(nm) {
  d <- fs_param_provenance(.fits[[nm]])
  d <- d[d$status == "differs from default", c("parameter", "default", "value_used")]
  if (nrow(d)) cbind(fit = nm, d) else NULL
}))
gt::gt(.pp, groupname_col = "fit") |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title = "Parameters differing from package defaults, by fit",
    subtitle = sprintf("forestsearch %s, read from args_call_all at render time.",
                       tryCatch(as.character(utils::packageVersion("forestsearch")),
                                error = function(e) "version unknown"))) |>
  gt::cols_label(parameter = "Parameter", default = "Package default",
                 value_used = "Value used") |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(font = gt::google_font("JetBrains Mono"), size = "x-small"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = c(default, value_used))) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = gt::px(11), data_row.padding = gt::px(2))
```

# Reproducibility payload (Section 6.2) {#sec-export-payload-gbsg}

The chunk below harvests the already-computed objects from the three engine runs
into one small list and writes it as an `.rds` for the manuscript Section 6.2
reader document to reproduce the table and the results overview. No analysis is
repeated; the output path, core count, and package version resolve at run time.

```{r export-section6-2-payload}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

.out_dir <- if (is.null(results_dir)) {
  tryCatch(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), error = function(e) getwd())
} else {
  results_dir
}
dir.create(.out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

.get <- function(nm) if (exists(nm, inherits = TRUE)) get(nm, inherits = TRUE) else NULL

.triple <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || is.null(x$est)) c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_) else c(x$est, x$lower, x$upper)
}
.fb_triple <- function(est_list) {
  if (is.null(est_list)) c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_) else c(est_list$H2, est_list$H2_lower, est_list$H2_upper)
}

.engine_rows <- function(method, fit, boot) {
  if (is.null(fit) || is.null(fit$mr_inference)) return(NULL)
  g  <- fit$mr_inference
  cc <- g$complement
  tr <- fit$df.est$treat.recommend
  n_tot <- length(tr); n_H <- sum(tr == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  nv_H  <- .triple(g$naive)
  nv_Hc <- .triple(if (!is.null(cc)) cc$naive)
  mr_H  <- .triple(g$debiased)
  mr_Hc <- .triple(if (!is.null(cc)) cc$debiased)
  fb_H  <- .fb_triple(if (!is.null(boot)) boot$H_estimates)
  fb_Hc <- .fb_triple(if (!is.null(boot)) boot$Hc_estimates)
  data.frame(
    method = method, region = c("H", "Hc"),
    n = c(n_H, n_tot - n_H),
    pct = round(100 * c(n_H, n_tot - n_H) / n_tot),
    naive_est = c(nv_H[1], nv_Hc[1]), naive_lo = c(nv_H[2], nv_Hc[2]), naive_hi = c(nv_H[3], nv_Hc[3]),
    fb_est = c(fb_H[1], fb_Hc[1]), fb_lo = c(fb_H[2], fb_Hc[2]), fb_hi = c(fb_H[3], fb_Hc[3]),
    mr_est = c(mr_H[1], mr_Hc[1]), mr_lo = c(mr_H[2], mr_Hc[2]), mr_hi = c(mr_H[3], mr_Hc[3]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

.engine_meta <- function(fit, boot_seconds) {
  if (is.null(fit) || is.null(fit$mr_inference))
    return(list(label = NA_character_, n_family = NA_integer_, selection_bias = NA_real_,
                boot_sec = NA_real_, mr_sec = NA_real_, speedup = NA_real_))
  g <- fit$mr_inference
  mr_sec <- if (!is.null(g$timing_seconds)) as.numeric(g$timing_seconds) else NA_real_
  list(label = paste(fit$sg.harm, collapse = " & "),
       n_family = g$n_family, selection_bias = g$selection_bias,
       boot_sec = boot_seconds, mr_sec = mr_sec,
       speedup = if (is.finite(boot_seconds) && is.finite(mr_sec) && mr_sec > 0) boot_seconds / mr_sec else NA_real_)
}

.tm <- .get("timings")
.boot_sec <- function(key) {
  v <- if (!is.null(.tm) && !is.null(.tm[[key]])) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.tm[[key]])) else NA_real_
  if (length(v) == 1L && is.finite(v)) v else NA_real_
}

# FS vs GRF agreement on the harm flag (treat.recommend == 0), aligned by id, with Cohen's kappa.
.concordance <- function(a, b, idn) {
  if (is.null(a) || is.null(b)) return(NULL)
  da <- a$df.est; db <- b$df.est
  if (is.null(da) || is.null(db) || !(idn %in% names(da)) || !(idn %in% names(db))) return(NULL)
  m <- merge(data.frame(.id = da[[idn]], ha = as.integer(da$treat.recommend == 0)),
             data.frame(.id = db[[idn]], hb = as.integer(db$treat.recommend == 0)), by = ".id")
  if (nrow(m) == 0L) return(NULL)
  po <- mean(m$ha == m$hb); pa <- mean(m$ha); pb <- mean(m$hb)
  pe <- pa * pb + (1 - pa) * (1 - pb)
  list(n_common = nrow(m), n_agree = sum(m$ha == m$hb), pct_agree = 100 * po,
       kappa = if (pe < 1) (po - pe) / (1 - pe) else NA_real_)
}

# Observed event rate by arm inside an engine's harm region (treat.recommend == 0).
# Cox analog of the binary version: the "rate" is the proportion experiencing the
# event (status == 1), reported alongside n and event counts so a reader can
# recompute incidence later if person-time is added.
.harm_rates <- function(fit, ename, tname) {
  if (is.null(fit) || is.na(ename) || is.na(tname)) return(NULL)
  d <- fit$df.est
  if (is.null(d) || !all(c(ename, tname, "treat.recommend") %in% names(d))) return(NULL)
  h <- d[d$treat.recommend == 0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(h) == 0L) return(NULL)
  et <- h[[ename]][h[[tname]] == 1]; ec <- h[[ename]][h[[tname]] == 0]
  list(treated_n      = length(et),
       control_n      = length(ec),
       treated_events = if (length(et)) sum(et == 1, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       control_events = if (length(ec)) sum(ec == 1, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_integer_,
       treated_pct    = if (length(et)) 100 * mean(et == 1, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
       control_pct    = if (length(ec)) 100 * mean(ec == 1, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_)
}

# Machine / hardware fingerprint of whatever computer ran this render, so that
# timings pooled across different machines stay attributable. Pure base R plus
# guarded platform calls (Linux / macOS / Windows); any field that cannot be
# determined returns NA rather than erroring.
.machine_info <- function(n_workers = NULL) {
  si   <- Sys.info()
  sn   <- unname(si[["sysname"]])               # "Linux" | "Darwin" | "Windows"
  sess <- tryCatch(sessionInfo(), error = function(e) NULL)

  .sys <- function(cmd) tryCatch(
    trimws(paste(system(cmd, intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE), collapse = " ")),
    error = function(e) NA_character_)

  cpu_model <- tryCatch({
    if (sn == "Linux") {
      ln <- grep("^model name", readLines("/proc/cpuinfo", warn = FALSE), value = TRUE)[1]
      if (length(ln) && !is.na(ln)) trimws(sub("^model name\\s*:\\s*", "", ln)) else NA_character_
    } else if (sn == "Darwin") {
      .sys("sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string")
    } else if (sn == "Windows") {
      out <- strsplit(.sys("wmic cpu get name"), "  +")[[1]]
      out <- out[nzchar(out) & out != "Name"]
      if (length(out)) out[length(out)] else NA_character_
    } else NA_character_
  }, error = function(e) NA_character_)

  ram_gb <- tryCatch({
    if (sn == "Linux") {
      kb <- as.numeric(sub("\\D*(\\d+).*", "\\1",
              grep("^MemTotal", readLines("/proc/meminfo", warn = FALSE), value = TRUE)[1]))
      round(kb / 1024^2, 1)
    } else if (sn == "Darwin") {
      round(as.numeric(.sys("sysctl -n hw.memsize")) / 1024^3, 1)
    } else if (sn == "Windows") {
      round(as.numeric(gsub("\\D", "", .sys("wmic ComputerSystem get TotalPhysicalMemory"))) / 1024^3, 1)
    } else NA_real_
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)

  list(
    hostname           = unname(si[["nodename"]]),
    user               = unname(si[["user"]]),
    os                 = if (!is.null(sess) && !is.null(sess$running)) sess$running else NA_character_,
    sysname            = sn,
    os_release         = unname(si[["release"]]),
    arch               = unname(si[["machine"]]),
    cpu_model          = if (length(cpu_model) == 1L) cpu_model else NA_character_,
    cores_physical     = tryCatch(parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE), error = function(e) NA_integer_),
    cores_logical      = tryCatch(parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE),  error = function(e) NA_integer_),
    cores_used         = if (!is.null(n_workers)) as.integer(n_workers) else NA_integer_,
    workers_registered = tryCatch(future::nbrOfWorkers(), error = function(e) NA_integer_),
    future_plan        = tryCatch(class(future::plan())[1], error = function(e) NA_character_),
    ram_gb             = if (length(ram_gb) == 1L) ram_gb else NA_real_,
    r_version          = R.version.string,
    r_platform         = R.version$platform,
    blas               = if (!is.null(sess) && !is.null(sess$BLAS)) sess$BLAS else NA_character_,
    lapack             = if (!is.null(sess) && !is.null(sess$LAPACK)) sess$LAPACK else NA_character_,
    timestamp          = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE)
  )
}

.fs      <- .get("fs");      .fs_bc      <- .get("fs_bc")
.fs_dina <- .get("fs_dina"); .fs_dina_bc <- .get("fs_dina_bc")
.fs_grf  <- .get("fs_grf");  .fs_grf_bc  <- .get("fs_grf_bc")

.meta_fs   <- .engine_meta(.fs,      .boot_sec("bootstrap"))
.meta_dina <- .engine_meta(.fs_dina, .boot_sec("fs_dina_bootstrap"))
.meta_grf  <- .engine_meta(.fs_grf,  .boot_sec("fs_grf_bootstrap"))

table1 <- do.call(rbind, list(
  .engine_rows("FS",   .fs,      .fs_bc),
  .engine_rows("DINA", .fs_dina, .fs_dina_bc),
  .engine_rows("GRF",  .fs_grf,  .fs_grf_bc)))

.dsel <- .get("dina_sel")
dina_standalone <- if (!is.null(.dsel) && isTRUE(.dsel$found)) {
  op <- if (identical(.dsel$direction, "left")) "<=" else ">="
  list(found = TRUE, label = sprintf("%s %s %s", .dsel$covariate, op, format(.dsel$threshold)), n = .dsel$n_subgroup)
} else {
  list(found = FALSE, label = NA_character_, n = NA_integer_)
}

.idname <- if (exists("id.name")) id.name else "id"
.oname  <- if (exists("outcome.name")) outcome.name else NA_character_
.ename  <- if (exists("event.name")) event.name else NA_character_
.tname  <- if (exists("treat.name")) treat.name else NA_character_

payload <- list(
  table  = table1,
  labels = list(fs = .meta_fs$label, dina = .meta_dina$label, grf = .meta_grf$label,
                dina_standalone = dina_standalone),
  meta   = list(
    B          = if (exists("NB")) NB else NA_integer_,
    mr_draws = if (exists("mr_draws")) mr_draws else NA_integer_,
    n_total    = if (!is.null(.fs)) nrow(.fs$df.est) else NA_integer_,
    cores      = tryCatch(unname(future::availableCores()), error = function(e) NA_integer_),
    machine    = .machine_info(n_workers = if (exists("n_cores")) n_cores else NULL),
    outcome    = .oname,
    event      = .ename,
    covariates = if (exists("confounders.name")) confounders.name else NA_character_,
    timings    = list(fs = .meta_fs, dina = .meta_dina, grf = .meta_grf)),
  extras = list(
    concordance = .concordance(.fs, .fs_grf, .idname),
    harm_rates  = .harm_rates(.fs, .ename, .tname)),
  est_scale = "hr",
  built_at  = Sys.time(),
  forestsearch_version = tryCatch(as.character(utils::packageVersion("forestsearch")), error = function(e) NA_character_))

# Payload filename -- analog of actg175's "actg175_table_payload.rds".
# (If your gbsg reader/manuscript doc expects "gbsg_table1_payload.rds", change it here.)
.payload_file <- file.path(.out_dir, "gbsg_survival_multimethod_payload.rds")
saveRDS(payload, .payload_file)
cat("Wrote Section 6.2 payload to:", .payload_file, "\n")
```
